channel.title: France 24 - International breaking news, top stories and headlines
channel.description: Breaking news and world news from France 24 on Business, Sports, Culture. Video news. News from the US, Europe, Asia Pacific, Africa, Middle East, America

item.title: Palantir CEO Alex Karp says French restrictions on US software are ‘backfiring’
item.description: Palantir CEO Alex Karp said on Wednesday French restrictions limiting government use of US-made software were proving counterproductive. His comments followed France’s decision to replace Palantir with domestic provider ChapsVision at intelligence agency DGSI over data sovereignty concerns. Karp said Europe’s regulatory environment was hurting competitiveness.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE 24

item.title: Venice Film Festival opens with George Clooney, Murdoch film and geopolitics
item.description: George Clooney used a Venice Film Festival appearance on Wednesday to weigh in on artificial intelligence, media ownership and US politics while receiving a lifetime achievement award. Clooney warned Hollywood must adapt to AI and criticised growing billionaire control of major media platforms.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE 24

item.title: Malta acquits tycoon Yorgen Fenech in investigative journalist's murder case
item.description: A Maltese court on Wednesday acquitted tycoon Yorgen Fenech of orchestrating the 2017 car-bomb killing of investigative journalist Daphne Caruana Galizia, a verdict that drew condemnation from her family and press freedom advocates. Her family said the acquittal denied Caruana Galizia justice, while her son called it a “terrible decision.”
item.dc:creator: FRANCE 24

item.title: Is Wintour still en vogue? Met navigates rough seas as Galliano retrospective sinks into 'Horizons'
item.description: François Picard is pleased to welcome Dana Thomas, author of Gods and Kings: The Rise and Fall of Alexander McQueen and John Galliano, and the New York Times bestseller Deluxe: How Luxury Lost Its Luster. The fiery controversy over the Met's now-cancelled John Galliano retrospective challenges the timeless debate over whether art can be separated from the artist. Our guest argues that the key issue is institutional power. From her perspective, Galliano’s stature as an artist and fashion designer is never in dispute. All the while, his character has been once again very publicly called into question.
item.dc:creator: François PICARD

item.title: Outrage as Maltese tycoon acquitted of reporter Daphne Caruana Galizia's murder
item.description: A Maltese court on Wednesday acquitted tycoon Yorgen Fenech of orchestrating the car-bomb killing of investigative reporter Daphne Caruana Galizia, sparking outrage from her family and media freedom advocates. The wealthy businessman had stood accused of masterminding the 2017 assassination of 53-year-old Caruana Galizia, which sparked unprecedented protests and brought down a government. MaltaToday Executive Editor Kurt Sansone speaks with FRANCE 24.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: US-Iran war: Old videos falsely claim to show new attacks on American bases
item.description: As US-Iran hostilities flare up and strikes has resumed, so has a wave of misinformation online. Old and unrelated videos are flooding social media, falsely presented as footage of new attacks. As tensions escalate, lips filmed in Dubai, Russia and the US have been misrepresented as Iranian strikes on US bases in the Gulf. Another 68-year-old video of a US nuclear test has been falsely claimed to show Iran detonating mines in the Strait of Hormuz. Vedika Bahl fact-checks in Truth or Fake.
item.dc:creator: Vedika BAHL

item.title: US oversees signing of ‘billions’ in deals between Venezuela and Chevron, ENI, GE
item.description: US oil giant Chevron, Italy's ENI and GE Vernova signed deals worth "tens of billions of dollars" with Venezuela, US Energy Secretary Chris Wright said Wednesday during a trip to Caracas where he and Interim President Delcy Rodriguez finalised the agreements.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE 24

item.title: Kenyan editor found safe after abduction
item.description: In tonight's edition, rights groups in Kenya call for an investigation after a top journalist is abducted overnight by heavily armed men. Also, trials for three potential vaccines against the Bunjeebuyyoo strain of Ebola are due to start over the next couple of months. And Senegalese consumers who are frustrated by the rising cost of living have launched a new campaign.
item.dc:creator: Georja CALVIN-SMITH

item.title: Chevron, Eni commit to expand oil projects in Venezuela under US eye
item.description: U.S.' Chevron, Italy's Eni and other foreign energy producers committed on Wednesday to major project expansions to boost oil output in Venezuela, in a signing ceremony in Caracas overseen by interim President ​Delcy Rodriguez and ‌U.S. Energy Secretary Chris Wright. FRANCE 24's Maya Yataghene reports.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: Zelensky warns airlines Russian skies not safe due to Ukraine drones
item.description: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky warned Tuesday that his country's drones would make Russia's airspace "completely unsafe" for the duration of the war, drawing accusations of "state terrorism" from Russian leader Vladimir Putin. Speaking with FRANCE 24's Mark Owen, Former British Military Intelligence Officer Philip Ingram explains that Zelensky's warning is addressed to "those international airlines from the Middle East, from South East Asia, China included that are still operating into Moscow" adding that "it's all part of the information war and bringing the overall conflict to the Russian people".
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: Spanish report flags Moroccan police's 'total permissiveness' in Ceuta migrant rush
item.description: Moroccan security forces displayed "total permissiveness" during last month's massive wave of migrants who crossed into the Spanish North African territory of Ceuta, according to a Spanish police report seen by a French news agency on Wednesday.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE 24

item.title: Israeli FM Gideon Sa'ar: 'I hope Iran will not make the mistake of attacking us'
item.description: In an interview with FRANCE 24, Israel's Minister of Foreign Affairs Gideon Sa’ar addressed the resumption in fighting between the US and Iran, and warned that any Iranian attack on Israel would trigger a "severe" response. He also accused Tehran of continuing to pursue "nuclear weapons aspirations", claiming that Israel "will not allow" Iran to achieve them.
item.dc:creator: Marc PERELMAN

item.title: Videos and debris raise questions over alleged US strike on Iranian wedding
item.description: On the evening of September 1, a barrage of US missile and drone attacks on a town in southern Iran allegedly struck a wedding ceremony, killing at least five people, including a four-year-old boy. FRANCE 24 geolocated a direct hit to the civilian building where local residents say the wedding was being held. The building was more than 135 meters from the apparent target, a communications tower.
item.dc:creator: The FRANCE 24 Observers

item.title: Russia blamed for explosive-laden drone found at German airport
item.description: After #Germany blamed #Russia for the explosive-laden #drone found at #Leipzig airport on August 4, #Berlin has introduced new sanctions against #Moscow. Namely, its consulate in #Bonn and the Russian House - a cultural centre thought to be a Russian #spy hub - in #Berlin.

item.title: Egypt welcomes Xi as Beijing expands influence in region
item.description: Egyptian ​President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi welcomed China's Xi Jinping to Cairo on Wednesday, opening a visit that highlights Cairo's deepening ties with Beijing as regional turmoil prompts U.S. allies to reassess longstanding security relationships.

item.title: Philippine couple married in hip-deep floodwaters
item.description: A Philippine couple tied the knot on Tuesday at a Catholic church swamped in hip-deep waters, as heavy rains had pummelled large parts of the country for a month.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: US postal whistleblower warns thousands of midterm ballots could be lost
item.description: A US Postal Service whistleblower has warned that millions of Americans could be prevented from receiving mail ballots ahead of November's midterm elections because of a rushed, new system ordered by President Donald Trump and due for launch Tuesday. Trump signed an executive order in March seeking tighter controls on mail voting, which he has repeatedly claimed is vulnerable to widespread fraud despite offering no evidence of misconduct on such a scale. France 24’s Kethevane Gorjestani takes a closer look.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: Search continues for tunnel workers in Nepal floods
item.description: Nepali authorities believe that the dozens of workers trapped in hydropower tunnels could still be alive, as some of the tunnels have chambers with air supplies. But rescue teams are still struggling, with difficult weather and heavy rains worsening the situation, reports France 24's Shahzaib Wahlah.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: Israel ‘organised and prepared’ to remove Gaza population if US gives green light, Katz says
item.description: Israel is "organised and prepared" to remove Palestininians from Gaza "by every way possible", Defence Minister Israel Katz told reporters Wednesday, adding that there was no alternative "solution" to crisis. The Israeli government was simply waiting for the US to figure out where to take the displaced Gazans, he said.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE 24

item.title: Paradox of Balladur's legacy: 'Highly popular' innovative Gaullist gradually became irrelevant
item.description: Sharon Gaffney is pleased to welcome Renaud Foucart, Senior Lecturer at Lancaster University. According to Foucart, Édouard Balladur’s political legacy mattered because he embodied a political model that was innovative and yet limited in scope and longevity. As PM under Socialist President François Mitterrand, Balladur helped demonstrate that ideological rivals could govern together under cohabitation while pursuing an ambitious programme of privatisation and economic reform. Yet Foucart argues that Balladur’s ultimately unsuccessful presidential campaign exposed a deeper transformation in French politics: technocratic competence, elite stature and institutional authority were becoming less electorally powerful than the ability to connect with ordinary voters.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24
